prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules, whether designed bifunctional degraders or molecular glues, induce proximity to the ubiquitin-proteasome system to remove chosen proteins

statement.case_for: After the round-1 exchange I keep a single-part prize for targeted protein degradation, and I keep Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli. The principle is a designed small molecule that forms a ternary complex and hands a chosen protein to the ubiquitin-proteasome system, so the protein is removed catalytically instead of occupied. That changes what chemists and clinicians can attempt, including targets without a druggable active site. It has been confirmed for two decades by many groups, ligases and targets. Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the concept with Sakamoto and Kim in 2001. Ciulli supplied the chemistry that made it a general design method: VHL ligands, the first fully small-molecule VHL-based degraders, and ternary-complex crystal structures that explain cooperativity and selectivity. I now propose a citation worded around induced proximity that names molecular glues, so the prize does not read as ignoring the one arm with approved drugs. Six of eight members already have B014 in their configuration. I treat that as agreement on the topic only, and I have tried to decide the citation and the third name on the science.
statement.case_against: The credit story cannot be made clean with three names. Handa and Ito (cereblon as the thalidomide target), Sakamoto and Kim (co-authors of the 2001 PROTAC paper) and Gray are all left out, and a citation that mentions glues while naming no glue discoverer is the weakest part of my own proposal. Clinical maturity is the second weakness: lenalidomide-class glues are approved, but no heterobifunctional degrader has an approval that I can confirm, so recognition of the PROTAC arm rests on mechanism, two decades of replication and trial activity. If the committee insists that the glue arm be anchored by a named discoverer, my configuration is the less defensible one and the Crews, Deshaies, Handa trio is the better choice.

responses.point: Linke asked what Ciulli discovered that is not already implied by Crews and Deshaies, and argued that Handa's cereblon work answers the clinical-maturity worry because induced proximity is already in approved drugs.
responses.response: My answer on Ciulli is three things. First, VHL ligands and the first fully small-molecule VHL-based degraders, which freed PROTACs from the peptide-based E3 recruiter of 2001 and made them cell-permeable and druggable. Second, crystal structures of ternary complexes and the demonstration of positive cooperativity, which turned the idea into something that can be optimised quantitatively. Third, selectivity (isoform selectivity beyond what the warhead binding predicts), which shows the principle is not just target binding. None of this is implied by the 2001 concept. I accept your clinical point about cereblon and I have moved part of the way: my citation now says induced proximity and names glues, which keeps the approved-drug evidence in the prize. I still do not think Handa's identification of cereblon is a design principle in the same sense, but I would not oppose Handa in place of Ciulli if the committee judges that clinical proof must be anchored by a name.

responses.point: Zou argues that Crews, Deshaies and Handa let one prize cover both the heterobifunctional and the molecular-glue arms, and admits the trio reads as two lineages stitched together.
responses.response: Zou states the weakness of that trio better than I could: Handa's work explains how an existing drug acts, while Crews and Deshaies give a general method for making new ones. I think the stitched-together reading is a real risk for a citation. I agree with the structural logic of cereblon reshaping a ligase surface, but the same logic is shown for VHL in Ciulli's ternary-complex structures, so the mechanism argument is not unique to the Handa choice. A broader citation does not need Handa's name to be accurate, though I accept that it then credits an approved-drug mechanism without the person who identified its target.

responses.point: Aqvist wants the citation to rest on the chemical principle and not on therapeutic outcomes, and wants the priority of Sakamoto and Kim in the 2001 paper confirmed before the names are final.
responses.response: I agree on the wording and my citation now contains no clinical claim, so the prize would not depend on the outcome of late-stage trials. On Sakamoto and Kim, I cannot check priority from the material in front of me. My reading is that Sakamoto and Kim were the first authors of the experimental work in the 2001 paper, with Crews and Deshaies as the conceptual and supervising leaders, but the three-name limit means they are left out whichever way we decide. I would rather say that openly than hide it. If the committee thinks first authorship of the founding experiment outweighs later design work, that changes my third name, and I want the committee to look at that question before the vote.

responses.point: Chabes proposes a two-part prize, B014 for Crews and Deshaies and B042 for Liu alone, so that two bench-to-chemistry tools are recognised and the Liu credit stays clean.
responses.response: I considered it seriously, since it fixes the credit problem for base editing and Liu's invention is clear. I do not follow it, for two reasons. First, it removes the third seat from B014, so the third name is the person whose absence is most debated. Second, as you say, two chemical-biology parts in one year are one neighbourhood twice, and base editing's relationship to the 2020 genome-editing prize and its short clinical record are open questions that I do not want to tie to the strongest candidate. Base editing remains my first alternative, and I would support Liu alone if the committee prefers two parts.

uncertainties: Whether Ciulli or Handa is the better third name, and whether a citation that names glues without naming a glue discoverer is honest.
Whether a prize for the PROTAC arm is premature without an approved heterobifunctional degrader. My recollection of trial status is unverified.
Priority and credit of Sakamoto and Kim in the 2001 PROTAC paper, and of Gray, Ito and others, none of whom are in my three.
Whether base editing (B042) is distinct enough from the CRISPR work recognised in 2020 to be a separate chemical invention.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict requiring recusal. My work on peptides, gold nanoparticles, biosensors and hydrogels does not overlap with any shortlisted candidate, and I have no personal or institutional tie to the candidates. My postdoc mentors Molly Stevens and Freddy Boey are not on the shortlist. Nothing in round 1 changes this disclosure.
